meta.description: U.S. tariff layers on goods of Canadian origin. Exposure on a shipment is the sum of every layer that applies. CUSMA qualification removes the MFN layer; it does NOT remove Section 232 or Section 338 duties.
meta.status: DRAFT - assembled from public secondary sources (law-firm and logistics advisories). Confirm every rate and HTS list against the Federal Register, CBP CSMS messages and the Trade Commissioner Service before launch, then on a fixed refresh schedule.

mfn.note: U.S. general (MFN) column-1 duty rates. Placeholder sample values by HS prefix for engine testing only. Production must load the full HTSUS from USITC (hts.usitc.gov) and match at 8-10 digits.

rates.description: Builders' joinery and carpentry of wood

programs.name: Section 232: steel and derivatives
programs.basis: Steel content value for derivative products; full value for listed steel articles.

programs.name: Section 232: aluminum and derivatives
programs.basis: Aluminum content value for derivative products.

programs.name: Section 232: softwood timber and lumber
programs.note: Separate from long-running softwood lumber anti-dumping/countervailing duties, which are company-specific and not modelled here.

programs.name: Section 232: upholstered furniture, kitchen cabinets and vanities
programs.note: Advisories report scheduled increases (30% upholstered, 50% cabinets/vanities) with conflicting effective dates.

programs.name: Section 232: automobiles and auto parts
programs.note: CUSMA-qualifying vehicles pay on non-U.S. content; qualifying parts have had exemptions. Route to expert review.

programs.name: Section 338: additional duties on listed Canadian goods
programs.authority: Section 338, Tariff Act of 1930 (proclamations of July 20, 2026)
programs.note: Three proclamations covering roughly 569 HTSUS lines across alcohol, dairy and other goods (reported to include some wood products, furniture, textiles, metals and machinery). The prefixes here are indicative only; production must load the exact HTSUS 8-digit annex lists.

inactive.name: IEEPA 'fentanyl' tariff on non-CUSMA Canadian goods (35%)
inactive.status: Invalidated by the U.S. Supreme Court (Learning Resources v. Trump, Feb 20, 2026); collection stopped Feb 24, 2026. Refund litigation ongoing.

inactive.name: Section 122 temporary import surcharge (10%)
inactive.status: Started Feb 24, 2026 with a 150-day statutory limit (around July 2026) unless extended by Congress. Current status unconfirmed.
